name: Iliofemoral (Smith-Petersen) approach to the hip (periprosthetic)
corridor: Anterior iliofemoral exposure developing the interval between tensor fasciae latae and sartorius superficially and releasing rectus femoris to reach the anterior hip and ilium

positioning.text: Position supine with the limb free for rotation and traction and a bump under the ipsilateral pelvis.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the lateral iliac crest and the anterior superior iliac spine.

incision.text: Begin the incision over the lateral iliac crest, follow it to the ASIS, then turn distally along the lateral border of the sartorius toward the patella.

superficial_interval.text: Develop the interval between the tensor fasciae latae and the sartorius, protecting the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve near the ASIS.

deep_interval.text: Identify, divide, and ligate the lateral femoral circumflex vessels distally, and release the direct head of rectus femoris from the anterior inferior iliac spine, taking the reflected head for more proximal exposure.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve, the tensor fasciae latae and sartorius interval, rectus femoris, the lateral femoral circumflex vessels, and the anterior hip capsule and ilium.

structures_at_risk.text: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve near the ASIS and the lateral femoral circumflex vessels are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The region just medial and distal to the ASIS is the danger zone for the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid vigorous medial retraction near the sartorius that stretches the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve.

exposure.text: Provides the most direct access to the anterior hip and the outer and inner tables of the ilium.

limitations.text: It gives poor access to the posterior column and is not commonly used for periprosthetic acetabular fractures.

indications.text: Indicated when direct anterior access to the hip and ilium is required, and it can be extended along the iliac crest.

closure.text: Repair the capsule, reattach the rectus femoris if released, repair the abductor origin, and close in layers over a subfascial drain.

complications.text: Complications include lateral femoral cutaneous nerve injury, hematoma from the circumflex vessels, and heterotopic ossification.

procedure_applications.condition: Direct anterior access to the hip and ilium is needed, though it is uncommon for periprosthetic acetabular fractures

questions.question: Along which muscle border does the Smith-Petersen incision turn distally?
questions.answer: Along the lateral border of the sartorius.
